## Name and persona

Each Familiar has a `name` and an optional `persona`, given to `familiars.create` and changed with `familiars.update`. Create Familiars once, on the first open.

- `persona` replaces the default, `defaultPersona(name)`, completely. Include the name if the model should know it.
- `hostInstructions`, a workspace option, is added after every persona, such as what your UI renders. Core adds its own instructions for rooms, memory, schedules and tools.

<Code code={customAssistant} lang="ts" title="assistant.ts" />

## Plugins

Core's own tools cover time, memory and schedules. A plugin adds yours: Pi Durable tools under a stable `name`, with a `title` for the Connections page and any `secrets` they share.

Import `defineTool` and `schema` from `@familiar-ai/core`, not your own copy of Pi, so they match the version Familiar runs:

<Code code={plugin} lang="ts" title="greeting.ts" />

Inside `execute`:

- `await familiar(context).author()` is the person whose message started the run, or a scheduled run's creator. It's `undefined` for background work. Use it to check rules such as who may change a task; every tool is available to everyone who talks to the Familiar.
- Pass `context.abortSignal` to anything you can cancel.
- `replay` defaults to `unsafe`. Mark a tool `safe` only if repeating it after a crash is harmless.

Each Familiar opts in to plugins: pass `capabilities` to `familiars.create`, set the workspace's `defaultCapabilities`, or call `setCapabilities` later.

## Secrets and network access

A plugin declares its secrets and exactly where each may be sent. The owner sets the value through the Connections API, and the plugin's code never sees it.

- `familiar(context).fetch(url)` is for requests that need no secret.
- `familiar(context).authorizedFetch(secret, url)` attaches the secret only if the request's origin, method and path match the declaration. Otherwise it throws without sending.

<Code code={connected} lang="ts" title="tasks.ts" />

A model can be talked into fetching any URL, so `fetch` must refuse private, loopback and tailnet addresses. On Node, Familiar's default does; in Workers and browsers, which can't reach them, it's the runtime's `fetch`. Pass your own `fetch` to `openWorkspace` only to change that.

These limits steer a well-behaved plugin. They don't contain one: a plugin runs in your process with its privileges. Install only plugins you trust.

## Tool details for UIs

A tool result has `output` for the model and optional `details`, JSON a UI can render, such as a card. It reaches the client as `ToolCall.details`, typed `unknown`, so check its shape and fall back to the text.

## MCP servers

The owner adds MCP servers at runtime through `workspace.mcp` or the `/mcp` routes, and turns each on per Familiar. HTTP servers connect through `mcpFetch`, which may reach private networks because the owner chose the endpoint. Local commands need an `mcpStdio` factory and run with your host's privileges; without one they show as failed. Restrict protocols, destinations and commands in those two.

To let a slow MCP tool report back later instead of holding up the reply, run it in the background:

```ts
await workspace.connections.updateToolSettings(
  { kind: 'mcp', name: 'topsail' },
  'watch_print',
  { runInBackground: true },
)
```

The Familiar replies while the call runs, then reports the result in the original room. **Ask first** approval still happens before the call starts.

## Data that belongs to your host

Keep your app's records in your app. Familiar's storage holds rooms, each Familiar's context, memory and schedules, and plugin secrets. Give tools your data through a plugin that calls your API, and check the author there.

`@familiar-ai/core/extensions` exports Pi Durable's types and helpers, such as `ToolExecutionApi`, at the bundled Pi version.
